model_annotation: Figure 4, titled “Zugewanderte und Personen mit Migrationshintergrund,” is a line chart comparing the labor force participation rates of two demographic groups in Germany over time: individuals who migrated to Germany by 2009 (represented by a light blue line with circular markers) and those who migrated by 2010 (represented by a dark blue line with square markers). The x-axis represents the year, ranging from 2005 to 2020, with tick marks at two-year intervals (2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2020). The y-axis represents the labor force participation rate as a percentage, ranging from 0% to 80%, with tick marks at 10% intervals. The light blue line begins at approximately 58% in 2005, rises gradually to about 62% by 2010, then continues increasing to roughly 68% by 2020. The dark blue line starts at approximately 52% in 2005, increases to about 58% by 2010, and reaches approximately 64% by 2020. Both lines show a consistent upward trend across the entire time period, with the light blue line consistently positioned above the dark blue line, indicating higher labor force participation among those who migrated by 2009 compared to those who migrated by 2010.
